title: Embeddings Explorer — UX sketch and dev notes
content:
Top-level idea:
Build a lightweight Embeddings Explorer UX for devs to iterate on index/embedding choices quickly — hyper local tool inside Console + standalone CLI web view. Primary users: ML engineers onboarding new models, infra folks debugging retrieval quality, product engineers evaluating semantic search for features.

Goals (what success looks like):
- < 5min to go from model selection -> qualitative view of nearest neighbors for a set of example queries.
- Fast compare: show side-by-side kd-tree/IVF/HNSW retrieval results across up to 3 indexes/models.
- Actions: label bad neighbors, pin correct matches, export subset as eval set.
- Integrates with Redwood API keys / private deployments (respecting KMS/air-gapped constraints).

Core flows (rough):
1) Quick probe: paste a short query or upload 10 sample queries -> see top-k neighbors + distances + source metadata.
2) Compare models: pick 2-3 models/quantization settings -> run same queries -> diff view highlighting changes (rank, score delta, new/removed).
3) Index diagnostics: show per-document vector norms, cluster assignments, and basic statistics (avg distance, density).
4) Build eval set: mark pairs as relevant/nonrelevant -> export CSV or push to project eval workspace.

Wireframe notes (very rough):
- Left panel: model/index selector, config toggles (normalize, use-nn-metric, batch-size, filter-by-tag).
- Middle pane: results list (source snippet, score, source id, tags) with inline actions (pin, label, open in raw doc view).
- Right pane: visualization space: small scatter t-SNE/UMAP for current query neighborhood, histogram of scores, cluster legend.
- Top bar: query input + batch upload + compare-toggle (view A vs view B).
- Footer: API call summary (tokens, latency, index queries, estimated $/1000 queries).

Developer ergonomics / integration points:
- Directly call /embeddings/search on chosen model and index via console proxy to respect routing/fallbacks.
- Option to replay request (record request -> replay against different model/quantization config).
- Built-in sample corpora: product docs, slack logs (sanitized), support tickets. Allow upload of CSV/JSONL.
- Local-only mode: for private/on-prem customers, explorer can run purely client-side against private endpoints.

User stories (prioritized):
- As an ML engineer, I want to paste a failing query and see why retrieval returns duplicates, so I can tune indexing or re-embed the doc.
- As a product engineer, I want to compare embeddings from model-v1 vs model-v2 on a set of user queries, so I can decide whether to roll forward.
- As an SRE, I want to surface slow index shards and average query latency per-shard, so I can triage hot spots.
- As a data annotator, I want to mark relevant pairs and export them for training an eval — minimal friction.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI can query a hosted model and display top-10 neighbors with metadata.
- Export labeled pairs as CSV and store a pointer to the export in Redwoods project storage.
- Compare mode shows rank deltas and score deltas for the same queries across 2 configs.
- Integrations: links to the underlying Github PR and a simple audit event emitted when a user exports labels.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: we must ensure example uploads are not cached in hosted logs for enterprise/private customers. (Need guidance from security on default retention and opt-out.)
- Cost: exploratory flows could generate a lot of embedding/rerank calls; need throttling + cost-visibility in UI.
- Visualizations: UMAP/t-SNE can be misleading for high-dim spaces; include clear disclaimers and toggles for different reduction algorithms.
- Large corpora: how to let users sample smartly (stratified or cluster-based sampling) so UI remains fast.

Technical notes / implementation hints:
- Backend: sequence: (1) embed queries -> (2) run index search -> (3) fetch doc snippets -> (4) compute any post-rerank. Keep these as separate observable steps in traces.
- Cache: local prefix caching of embeddings for repeated queries to speed iteration.
- Repro: store a small manifest for each experiment run (model, quantization, index config, timestamp) so replay is deterministic.
- API surface: add a lightweight debug endpoint: POST /debug/embeddings/run that returns neighbor ids + distances + trace ids. Keep it rate-limited and gated by team perms.

Prototype plan (3 sprints):
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): console-only alpha: embed query -> show neighbors -> simple export. Focus: dev ergonomics, minimal endpoint.
- Sprint 2 (3 weeks): compare-mode + visualization + replay manifest. Add cost-metering in footer.
- Sprint 3 (3 weeks): indexing diagnostics + sample corpora + private deployment adjustments (local-only mode). Add audit events and retention controls.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Check with Security: recommended retention policy for uploaded examples (Jira DX-318).
- Slack Alex (in #embeddings-experimentation) about reusing small sample corpora from support-export.
- Prototype UMAP with 2000-point limit; fallback to cluster-summary for larger sets.
- Draft quickstart in Console docs: 1) pick model, 2) paste query, 3) label/pin, 4) export.
- Add small telemetry event: explorer.session.start, explorer.run.compare, explorer.labels.export.

Relevant links and context:
- Related PR: embeds-explorer/pull/42 (early front-end scaffolding).
- Internal thread: slack thread "embedding model drift" (summary pinned by Maya).
- Inspiration: internal search playground from 2023 hackweek (low-latency neighbor preview).

Random brain dump ideas (unstructured):
- Quick "what changed" diff: show a single doc's embedding shift (arrow) when model changes. Could highlight docs that moved > threshold.
- Add a little "explain" widget: for each neighbor, show top-k tokens or chunk that contributed most to similarity (approx via dot contributions or gradient-based saliency). Might be noisy but useful.
- Allow teams to save an "experiment" preset: model, index, filter, sample set — can be shared via URL.

Finish: this is a working sketch — want to pair with Maya on the first wireframe and with Alex for the API contract. Keep it lightweight and biased toward iteration speed.

End of notes.
